opportunity: Power-resilience kits for Quebec municipal service and temporary-shelter centres
government_organization: Quebec local municipalities (1,108 covered by the regulation); MRCs
department: Municipal sécurité civile coordinator / fire service
requirement: Municipality must be able to cope with a power interruption at designated service and temporary-shelter centres
hazard_scenario: 24h-7d grid outage (ice storm, derecho); centre opens dark or runs on an undersized generator
product_category: Turnkey bilingual kit: LiFePO4 power stations, solar input, LED area lighting, multi-device charging bar, CO alarms, cords, signage, deployment card, yearly readiness check
government_evidence: RLRQ c. S-2.4, r.1 (in force for all local municipalities since 9 Nov 2019); MSP guide says centres must withstand an outage, e.g. generator plus fuel; Fiona: designated comfort centre had no generator (Glace Bay)
existing_procurement: Ad hoc: standby generators bought as capital projects; little evidence of packaged, portable centre kits
procurement_frequency: Event-driven plus budget cycle (Oct-Dec budget adoption, Q1 spend)
current_supplier: Fragmented: local electrical contractors, Canadian Tire / Costco retail, generator dealers
contract_value: $8K-$30K per municipality (1-3 kits); sub-threshold, so invitation or gré à gré under the municipality's own contract rules (VERIFY current thresholds)
procurement_method: Direct purchase / invitation below threshold; UMQ or FQM group purchasing as the scale path
procurement_gap: Rule exists, but no standard product; most municipalities are small and have no engineer to specify one
potential_manufacturer: Power stations: Canadian-assembled LiFePO4 line (e.g. Hybrid Power Solutions, Ontario) or a tier-1 brand via its Canadian distributor; lighting and CO alarms from a Canadian electrical wholesaler
potential_distributor: Quebec electrical wholesaler (Lumen, Guillevin, Nedco class): VERIFY government-account terms
potential_gov_price: $8,500-$11,000 per kit plus $900-$1,500 a year readiness service (ESTIMATE)
net_margin: 18-25% after freight, insurance, French documentation, overhead
capital_required: $5K-$15K (pilot kits and documentation); then order-by-order on Net-30 terms
supplier_financing: Ask the distributor for Net-30/60 and drop-ship. BDC purchase-order loans need 12+ months of revenue, so they are not available in year 1
contract_structure: Equipment sale + 3-year readiness service (inspection, battery cycling, exercise support)
relationship_pathway: MRC civil-security coordinators -> municipal coordinators -> UMQ/FQM purchasing -> MSP regional directorates (sessions, not sales)
recompete_date: Budget window: approach Sep-Nov for next-year budgets; spring before the summer storm season
probability_of_winning: Medium-High (first 5 sales); Medium for a group-purchasing listing
next_action: Pull the Légis Québec text of r.1 (s.10 onward), build one demo kit on paper, call 5 MRC coordinators to test the pain point

opportunity: Pre-positioned outage and evacuation caches for remote First Nations communities (Indigenous-led joint venture)
government_organization: Indigenous Services Canada; First Nations band councils; tribal councils
requirement: Shift from reactive response to preparedness; community-level capacity
hazard_scenario: Multi-day outage in diesel-grid or long-line communities; wildfire evacuations; winter-road isolation
product_category: Community cache: battery and solar power, heating-safe supplies, lighting, comms charging, water storage, managed and rotated in the community
government_evidence: OAG 2022 Report 8: ISC spent 3.5x more on response than on preparedness (~$828M over 4 yrs); recommended risk-based investment in preparedness. OAG Oct 2025 follow-up: 560+ emergencies, ~150 evacuations 2023-25
existing_procurement: Generators called up off the PSPC standing offer (ISC contract 4500481789, May 2025); generator servicing for 26 remote health facilities
procurement_frequency: Annual EMAP and preparedness funding cycles; event-driven reimbursements
current_supplier: Generator NMSO holders; regional suppliers; Canadian Red Cross under agreements
contract_value: $25K-$150K per community; band-council purchases with ISC funds (ESTIMATE)
contract_expiry: Funding cycles follow the fiscal year (Apr-Mar)
procurement_method: Band-council procurement (not bound by federal rules); ISC contracts; PSIB set-asides for a qualifying Indigenous business
procurement_gap: Preparedness is acknowledged as underfunded; logistics are too remote and too small for national suppliers
potential_manufacturer: Same power and lighting stack as G01; cold-rated LiFePO4 required (low-temperature charging cut-off)
potential_distributor: Northern logistics carriers (air and winter road), community-based storage
est_landed_cost: Freight can be 15-40% of product cost (VERIFY by route)
capital_required: $10K-$30K; freight prepay is the cash risk
supplier_financing: Progress payments or deposits are common with band councils; negotiate 30-50% deposit
contract_structure: Joint venture led by an Indigenous partner with real ownership and control (PSIB rules; anything else is fronting and is fraud)
relationship_pathway: Tribal council emergency coordinators; Indigenous business partner; ISC regional EM offices
recompete_date: Engage Jan-Mar for April fiscal-year planning; before wildfire season
probability_of_winning: Medium (with a real partner); Low without one
next_action: Read OAG 2022 Report 8 and the 2025 follow-up; find 2-3 Indigenous-owned suppliers interested in a genuine partnership
